subject: Game Theory
title: Divorce Settlements
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Divorce Settlements.

hook.text: Divorce splits a shared life into two. Assets, custody, and alimony all become bargaining chips.

buildup.text: Each side has private information about income, savings, and future plans—all of which affect fair division.

discovery.text: Lawyers serve as agents, but their incentives may differ from their clients': more conflict means more fees.

twist.text: Custody battles are rarely zero-sum. Creative arrangements—shared time, flexible schedules—create integrative gains.

climax.text: Mediation tends to produce better outcomes than litigation: lower cost, faster resolution, higher satisfaction.

punchline.text: The best divorces negotiate, not litigate.

quiz.question: Why might lawyers' incentives conflict with clients' in divorce?
options: More conflict can mean more fees
